content: 1. Spectinomycin hydrochloride is not effective in treating syphilis. 2. The use of high doses of antibiotics for short durations to treat gonorrhea may mask or delay the symptoms of incubating syphilis. 3. Since syphilis requires prolonged therapy with an effective antibiotic, patients being treated for gonorrhea should be closely monitored clinically. 4. All patients diagnosed with gonorrhea should undergo a serologic test for syphilis at the time of diagnosis. 5. Patients treated with spectinomycin hydrochloride should have a follow-up serologic test for syphilis three months after treatment. 6. Spectinomycin contains benzyl alcohol, which has been associated with a fatal Gasping Syndrome in premature infants and an increased incidence of neurologic and other complications. Precautions: 7. Standard precautions should be observed in individuals with a history of atopy. 8. The clinical effectiveness of Trobicin Sterile Powder should be monitored to detect the development of resistance by Neisseria gonorrhoeae. 9. Prescribing Trobicin Sterile Powder in the absence of a confirmed or strongly suspected bacterial infection, or without a prophylactic indication, is unlikely to benefit the patient and increases the risk of developing drug-resistant bacteria. Information for Patients: 10. Patients should be informed that antibacterial drugs, including Trobicin Sterile Powder, should only be used to treat bacterial infections and not viral infections (e.g., the common cold). 11. When prescribed Trobicin Sterile Powder for a bacterial infection, patients should be advised to take the medication exactly as directed, even if they feel better early in the course of therapy. 12. Skipping doses or failing to complete the full course of therapy may: Decrease the effectiveness of the immediate treatment. Increase the likelihood of bacteria developing resistance, making them untreatable by Trobicin Sterile Powder or other antibacterial drugs in the future. Carcinogenesis, Mutagenesis, Impairment of Fertility: 13. The genotoxicity of spectinomycin hydrochloride was evaluated in six assay systems, including two Ames tests, two micronucleus tests in mice, unscheduled DNA synthesis in rat primary hepatocytes, and a chromosomal aberration test in Chinese hamster ovary cells. 14. Spectinomycin was not found to be mutagenic or genotoxic in these tests. 15. No adverse effects on fertility or general reproductive performance were observed when spectinomycin was administered subcutaneously to rats at doses up to 300 mg/kg (equivalent to the recommended maximum human dose based on mg/m²). 16. A three-generation reproduction study in rats, with oral administration of spectinomycin hydrochloride at doses up to 400 mg/kg (equivalent to the recommended maximum human dose based on mg/m²), showed no evidence of drug-induced toxicity during growth, gestation, or lactation periods of any parental generation. 17. Pregnancy rates in the 400 mg/kg/day groups were consistently lower than those in the control groups. 18. Histopathological examination of the testes and ovaries of the third-generation animals was normal. Pregnancy Category: B 19. Spectinomycin was not teratogenic or embryocidal when administered orally or subcutaneously to rats at doses of 300 mg/kg/day (equivalent to the recommended maximum human dose based on mg/m²). 20. No teratogenic effects were observed when spectinomycin was administered intraperitoneally to mice or rats at doses of 400 or 1600 mg/kg/day, respectively. 21. Spectinomycin was administered intramuscularly or subcutaneously to pregnant rabbits at doses up to 300 mg/kg/day (equivalent to the recommended maximum human dose based on mg/m²), and embryonic and fetal development were unaffected by treatment. 22. Since there are no controlled studies of spectinomycin in pregnant women, and because animal reproduction studies are not always predictive of human responses, spectinomycin should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. Nursing Mothers: 23. It is not known whether spectinomycin is excreted in human milk. 24. Since many drugs are excreted in human milk, caution should be exercised when spectinomycin is administered to a nursing woman. Pediatric Use: 25. The safety and effectiveness of spectinomycin in the pediatric population have not been established.
